source_reviews.independent_solution: Superposition of overlapping coherent light waves produces phase-dependent reinforcement and weakening, giving a stable bright-dark distribution. For compatible polarizations I=I1+I2+2sqrt(I1 I2)cos(delta). In phase reinforces; opposite phase weakens, with complete cancellation only for equal amplitudes. A dark region is not destroyed energy; energy flow is redistributed. In an ideal nonabsorbing antireflection system, reduced reflection increases transmission.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Differences in single-frequency colour are associated with frequency. A stationary interface leaves frequency unchanged while speed and wavelength may change, so cross-medium wavelengths alone do not decide colour.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Under suitable illumination, a sufficiently thin air gap in ice can produce overlapping reflections from its two boundaries. Extra optical path depends on thickness and angle; different frequencies in white light are reinforced or weakened differently, yielding coloured glints. This is conditional, not guaranteed for every fracture, and is an explanation rather than a request to make cracks. With n_ice>n_air, the ice-to-air reflection has no pi reversal while the air-to-ice reflection has one: relative reflection phase pi. At normal incidence delta=4pi*n_air*h/lambda0+pi, so ideal reflected maxima occur at 2*n_air*h=(m+1/2)*lambda0 and minima at 2*n_air*h=m*lambda0. The coating's quarter-wave cancellation rule cannot simply be transferred to this reversed index ordering.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Principal applications here are interferometric precision measurements and tests, including wavelength and gas refractive index from optical-path/fringe changes, and antireflection treatment of optical glass. Coatings arrange opposite relative phase and matched reflected amplitudes to reduce reflection and stray light. With two low-to-high reflections, reflection phase changes cancel relatively; the thinnest normal-incidence choice is h=lambda_film/4, with complete cancellation only for equal amplitudes. One optimum thickness does not cancel all white-light frequencies, and real absorption cannot be ignored.
